text:
irene: quick heads-up — noticed the cost dashboard is showing cache savings that all get attributed to the first model in a chain. e.g. A -> B -> C, prefix hit on B but savings are applied to A's token cost. feels wrong for per-model/unit econ. any objections to changing attribution to the "invocation_path" that actually used the cached KV?
samir: oof yea i've seen that. current pipeline only records first_route in the trace and we do prefix crediting at billing join time. changing will touch proxy, telemetry and the billing join.
chloe: can we add a 'kv_owner' field to the request-level event instead of reworking joins? so billing can decide attribution later. that keeps proxy simple.
irene: that was my thought too — emit `kv_owner_route` when cache returns a hit. then billing can split credits: owner gets majority, origin route gets a small prefetch credit.
rafael: curious about corner cases: what if cached kv is shared (prefetch across routes) or a multi-tenant dedicated pool? how do we avoid double-crediting?
chloe: propose rule set: if `kv_owner_route` == origin_route -> full credit to origin. if different and `shared_kv=true` -> split 50/50 unless route has canary tag then route gets 70/30. arbitrary but easy to explain.
nina: 50/50 seems risky. ops asked for tenant-level accountability. maybe default is credit owner unless origin route explicitly requested prefetch via header `x-prefetch-invocation=true`. then origin gets prefetch credit.
samir: that implies changing client SDKs or internal callers to mark prefetch. we can also infer prefetch by short TTL and immediate subsequent calls but that's heuristic.
irene: okay practical plan proposal: 1) telemetry: add `kv_owner_route` and `cache_mode` (`explicit_prefetch` | `implicit_prefetch` | `shared`) to cache_hit events. 2) billing join: prefer explicit prefetch credit to origin, else credit owner. 3) provide a reconciliation report for first 7 days to surface anomalies.
platform-bot: deploy plan created: `kanban/card/4129` — wait for approvals from @samir and @rafael.
rafael: i'm +1 for that plan. want also an opt-in toggle for strict_owner_credit for Dedicated customers (enterprise request).
chloe: UX ask: in console cost breakdown, add a new row: "cache credit (owner vs origin)" and a tooltip explaining rules. can we add sample SQL for the finance team?
irene: sample SQL (pseudo):
```
SELECT route, sum(tokens) as tokens, sum(token_cost) - sum(cache_credit) as net_cost
FROM billing_events
GROUP BY route
```
we'll add `cache_credit_owner`, `cache_credit_origin` columns.
nina: agree, and let's include a nightly job that flags routes where >30% of credit flows to other routes. catches misconfigurations.
samir: timeline: I'll prototype telemetry change this week, chloe can mock console widget next sprint, billing join change scheduled for next release after a short audit.
irene: sounds good. tagging for follow-ups: @chloe to mock UX, @samir to open telemetry PR, @rafael to confirm enterprise toggle requirements. thanks all :thumbsup:
platform-bot: note: `audit-log` entry created for thread 2487654321.
